sections.h2: Which McKee offices touch a Jackson County tax bill?
sections.html:
Three courthouse-area offices share the work: the PVA values land and buildings, the Sheriff collects, and the Clerk keeps the land records. The county's officials page lists each one.

  • PVA, P.O. Box 249, McKee, KY 40447, phone (606) 287-7634, fax (606) 287-7079. It maintains property records and assesses property.
  • Sheriff, P.O. Box 426, McKee, KY 40447, phone (606) 287-7121. The county names tax collection among its duties.
  • County Clerk, P.O. Box 339, McKee, KY 40447, phone (606) 287-7800. It records deeds and mortgages and processes transfers.

The county site gives phone numbers and not a payment portal, so call the Sheriff to learn which payment methods and counter hours apply.

sections.h2: What dates matter for a Jackson County bill?
sections.html:
The statewide calendar governs. KRS 134.015 sets December 31 as the due date and gives a 2 percent discount to anyone who pays in full by November 1.

The regular Kentucky collection stages that Jackson County follows (source: KRS 134.015)
When paidResult
By November 12 percent off
November 2 through December 31Printed amount
January5 percent added
February onward10 percent added

If mailing slips, the Department of Revenue may set an alternative schedule with a month for each stage. The Sheriff stops collecting on April 15 and the Clerk takes the unpaid bills. Call the Sheriff if a bill never arrives, since a missing bill does not cancel a penalty.

sections.h2: What is the route for disputing a Jackson County value?
sections.html:
Ask the PVA for a conference. KRS 133.120 treats that conversation as a required first step, held before or during the inspection period, with a phone option on request.

If the conference leaves you unsatisfied, send the County Clerk a written petition. It should explain your reasons, identify the parcel and give your opinion of fair cash value, and it is due one workday after the inspection period closes. Rural owners should plan ahead, because the bill itself arrives too late to contest.

A public hearing before the board of assessment appeals follows. Gather these before you go:

  • A description of the land and buildings.
  • Insurance policies and construction costs.
  • Listings, contracts or a recent appraisal.
  • Loan or mortgage papers on the parcel.

The board may deny an appeal that lacks supporting facts. Tax remains payable on your claimed value during the case.

sections.h2: How much of a Jackson County house does the homestead exemption cover?
sections.html:
A lot of it. The deduction of $49,100 for the 2025 and 2026 assessment years meets a Census typical home value of $111,500 here, leaving $62,400 to tax. That cuts the taxable base by about 44 percent.

Applicants must be 65 or older, or totally disabled under a federal or retirement-system program, and must live in the home. Take a birth certificate, driver's license or passport to the PVA as proof of age. Disabled owners usually reapply every year, except veterans with a service-connected disability and those found permanently disabled by Social Security or Kentucky Retirement Systems.

The deduction follows the owner's own residence. A seller who moves out should notify the PVA and file again for the new address.

sections.h2: What if tax is still owed when a Jackson County house sells?
sections.html:
Plan to pay it from proceeds. The tax is a personal debt from the assessment date, the lien on the land can last 11 years, and after April 15 the Clerk files the bill as a certificate of delinquency.

The Department of Revenue lays out the sequence. The County Attorney mails a first notice within 30 days and, where needed, a second one within 60. KRS 134.128 puts the tax sale between 90 and 135 days after the transfer, and the Clerk advertises the list 30 to 45 days ahead.

Revenue's worked example shows what waiting costs. A $1,000 bill turns into a $1,254 certificate at transfer and $1,659.90 if paid after the June advertisement. Those figures rest on assumed commissions, so call the Jackson County Clerk at (606) 287-7800 for the real total.

sections.h2: Who records the deed, and what tax applies?
sections.html:
The County Clerk in McKee records it. That office also issues vehicle and marriage licenses and keeps wills and notary bonds, and it collects the state transfer tax before accepting a deed.

KRS 142.050 charges the grantor 50 cents per $500 of value. For the $111,500 Census value that is exactly 223 units, or $111.50. Exemptions cover gifts of nominal value, spouses in a divorce and foreclosure transfers, among others.

Call the Clerk for the current recording fee before closing, because the amount is set by statute and can change.

sections.h2: What is it like to sell a home in Jackson County?
sections.html:
Jackson County sits where the Cumberland Plateau meets the Bluegrass, with ground from about 600 to 1,600 feet above sea level. It was formed in 1858 from parts of Madison, Estill, Owsley, Clay, Laurel and Rockcastle counties. McKee is the seat, and Annville is the largest community.

Some 56,000 acres, about a quarter of the county, belong to the Daniel Boone National Forest, and the Sheltowee Trace trail has a trailhead in McKee. US 421 runs north toward Berea and Richmond and south toward Manchester. KY 30 links the county to I-75 and the Mountain Parkway. There is no hospital in the county, so residents drive to Berea, Richmond, London or Manchester.

  • 13,325 residents in 2025, up 2.8 percent from 2020.
  • 345.2 square miles of land, about 37.5 people per square mile.
  • 77.4 percent of homes occupied by their owners.
  • $665 median gross rent and $40,000 median household income.
  • A mean commute of 37.7 minutes.

Three industrial parks, in Annville, McKee and Sandgap, anchor local jobs, and the Jackson County Fair and Homecoming runs the weekend before Labor Day. Jackson Energy supplies power, and the Jackson County Water Association serves homes outside McKee.

faqs.q: Where do I find the Jackson County PVA?
faqs.a: In McKee. The mailing address is P.O. Box 249, McKee, KY 40447, and the office phone is (606) 287-7634.

faqs.q: What is the discount for paying early?
faqs.a: Two percent, if you pay in full by November 1 under KRS 134.015. From November 2 through December 31 the printed amount is due.

faqs.q: What does a late payment cost?
faqs.a: Five percent in January and 10 percent after January 31. A bill still open on April 15 moves to the Clerk, where 1 percent monthly interest and commissions start.

faqs.q: Can a seller keep the homestead exemption after leaving?
faqs.a: Only on the home where the seller lives. After closing, tell the PVA and file for the new residence.

faqs.q: Is the deed recorded at the McKee courthouse?
faqs.a: Yes, with the County Clerk, who records deeds and mortgages and collects the 50 cents per $500 transfer tax. Phone (606) 287-7800 to confirm current fees.
